info.title: Masia relay
info.description: The open Masia relay: orders MLS commits per conversation (the epoch serializer), stores signed device lists and key packages, and delivers ciphertext it cannot read.

bearerAuth.description: EdDSA (Ed25519) access token from the host API, named by its `kid` header: { iss, aud, sub: userId, did: deviceId, role?: "FAMILY_ADMIN", adminOf?: userId[], guardianOf?: userId[], iat, exp }. `iss` and `aud` must equal the relay's configured RELAY_TOKEN_ISSUER and RELAY_TOKEN_AUDIENCE. Lives at most 10 minutes; `iat` and `exp` are checked with 30 seconds of clock tolerance. `role` alone grants nothing: an admin acts only on the users listed in `adminOf` (never the admin themself), and a guardian device only for the children listed in `guardianOf` (each list at most 64; a list without the role is refused).

post.summary: Register the calling device, or refresh its label
post.description: The id must equal the `did` of the token. Keys, role and owner are fixed once registered; only `name` and `platform` can change. 201 when new, 200 when refreshed. `userId` is the account the device belongs to (default: the token's user). A USER device belongs to the token's user. A GUARDIAN device belongs to the CHILD it guards: `userId` is the child, who must be listed in the token's `guardianOf`. An ASSISTANT device is registered only by the relay's operator principal, for itself. Anything else is 403 ROLE_FORBIDDEN. `identityKeyPub` of a USER or ASSISTANT device is the ACCOUNT's identity key (the key that signs its device list; for the operator, the operator key): the first USER or ASSISTANT device pins it for the user, every later device of either role must carry the same key, else 409 IDENTITY_KEY_CHANGED. A GUARDIAN device neither pins nor must match. Only the explicit reset (`DELETE /users/{userId}/identity-key`) releases the pin. The 409 carries the pinned key as `identityKeyPub` (base64), because a second device cannot read it any other way before it is registered: it registers again with that key. Only the account's own token reaches that answer (a USER device is registered for the token's user alone, an ASSISTANT device only by the operator for itself), so it tells an account its own public key.

get.summary: A user's devices that are not revoked
get.description: Your own devices, and those of a user you administer (`adminOf`), come in full. Anyone else's come only as `{ id, role, identityKeyPub, signatureKeyPub }`, and only when the calling device shares (or shared) a room with one of that user's devices (403 NOT_A_CONTACT otherwise): the relay's only notion of a contact. The operator's devices (the account that owns every ASSISTANT device) come as public rows to every device. The same gate guards the signed device list and the key-package claim; a user named in the token's `reach` claim (the host's introduction) counts as a contact. `identityKeyPub` beside `rows` is the account's pinned identity key (null when none is pinned; the operator's is pinned by its first ASSISTANT device, so it is never null once one is registered): the key a correspondent pins (TOFU) and verifies the signed device list with. The gate is checked first; the lookup budget is shared with `GET /users/:userId/device-list` and is spent only by lookups that could be part of a walk through the user ids: your own devices, those of a user you administer and those of a user you share a room with cost nothing; the operator's cost the calling user's budget; a user reached through the token's `reach` claim costs the calling user's budget and the target's; a refused stranger (403) costs the calling user's budget (per calling user 120, per target user 120, per 10 minutes; 429 with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Revoke a device so it can no longer act
post.description: Allowed for another device of the same user, or for a FAMILY_ADMIN token whose `adminOf` lists the device's user. A device that does not exist and a device the caller may not revoke get the same 403 REVOKE_FORBIDDEN. ADR-117 §5a: revoking a token does not remove an MLS leaf, so the client MUST have committed MLS Remove for this device in every room first (Remove, then revoke). The relay holds the line: while the device is still a member of any room the answer is 409 STILL_IN_ROOMS. Revoking an already-revoked device is a no-op that returns it.

delete.summary: Release an account's pinned identity key (the explicit reset)
delete.description: The «new person to the cryptography» flow (canon §3): after it, the account's next USER or ASSISTANT device pins a fresh identity key and every correspondent sees a key change. Host-driven: only a FAMILY_ADMIN token whose `adminOf` lists the user (never the caller themself: the operator principal's own device is still active behind its token, so it cannot reset its own key), and only once every USER and ASSISTANT device of the account is revoked (409 IDENTITY_KEY_IN_USE with `devices` otherwise; GUARDIAN devices do not count). Anyone else gets 403 REVOKE_FORBIDDEN. A user with no pin is a no-op. The reset also discards the account's signed device list and every stored version of it: the next key starts a new chain at version 1, so no reader is served a version signed by the released key.

post.summary: Store the caller's signed device list
post.description: ADR-117 §2a. The relay stores the list exactly as the client signed it and never signs it itself. It applies two rules. The version must be the stored version + 1 (the first list is version 1), else 409 with `currentVersion`. The signature must verify under the account's pinned identity key over the canonical `mls-device-list/v1` bytes, else 422 DEVICE_LIST_SIGNATURE_INVALID (`reason` is `BAD_SIGNATURE`, or `NO_PINNED_KEY` when the account has no pinned key yet: register a device first); every reader verifies the whole chain of versions, so one version nobody can verify would block all of them. Entries that cannot be signed in that format (a key that is not 32 bytes, an ASSISTANT entry without its conversation) are 422 DEVICE_LIST_ENTRY_INVALID. Every version is kept (append-only, `GET /users/{userId}/device-list/versions`). A `conversationId` is accepted on an ASSISTANT entry only (422 DEVICE_LIST_ENTRY_INVALID otherwise).

get.summary: A user's current signed device list
get.description: Clients verify the signature against the user's pinned identity key; the relay checked it once, when the list was stored, but is not trusted for it. Readable by the owner, by an admin of the owner (`adminOf`) and by a contact: a device that shares (or shared) a room with one of the owner's devices. The operator's list (the account that owns every ASSISTANT device) is readable by every device. Anyone else gets 403 NOT_A_CONTACT, the same for a user who exists and one who does not. The gate is checked first, then the lookup budget (429 with `Retry-After`) that the relationship prices: your own list, the list of a user you administer and that of a user you share a room with cost nothing (an open client re-reads those about once a minute on every device); the operator account costs the calling user (120 per 10 minutes across all of their devices, 429 ACTOR_RATE_LIMITED) and no target budget, so nobody can make it unreachable for the others; a user reached through the token's `reach` claim costs the calling user and the target (120 across all callers, 429 TARGET_RATE_LIMITED); a refused stranger (403) costs the calling user, so a walk through the user ids stops after one budget.

get.summary: Every stored version of a user's signed device list newer than `afterVersion`
get.description: The relay keeps every version (append-only). A member that pinned version N passes `afterVersion=N` and verifies each row, oldest first, against the pinned identity key: the rows are exactly what the owner uploaded, so the client rebuilds the signed `mls-device-list/v1` bytes from them. `nextCursor` is the last version on the page (pass it as `afterVersion`), null on the last page; at most 64 rows a page. A user with no list (or none newer) is an empty page. Same contact gate (403 NOT_A_CONTACT) and same lookup budget and pricing as `GET /users/{userId}/device-list`.

post.summary: Upload key packages for the calling device
post.description: The body is an array of MLS KeyPackages (as MLSMessages). The relay reads each one's lifetime from its cleartext: an unreadable package is 422 KEY_PACKAGE_UNREADABLE (with `index`, `field`, `reason`), an expired one 422 KEY_PACKAGE_EXPIRED; expired packages are never served and are purged. After the upload the device must own at least one unexpired last-resort package (kept even when the pool is empty, never consumed), else 422 LAST_RESORT_REQUIRED, and at most 200 unclaimed packages, else 409 KEY_PACKAGE_POOL_FULL; either refusal rolls the whole upload back. Uploads are limited to 20 per device and 60 per user per 10 minutes (429 UPLOAD_RATE_LIMITED, `Retry-After`). A package the device already holds (the same bytes, spent or not) is skipped, not stored twice, and not counted in `uploaded`, so a retried upload is safe and answers `uploaded: 0` with the same `available`: an MLS KeyPackage is single use and must never reach two claimers. `available` is how many ordinary packages remain.

post.summary: Claim one key package per active device of a user, or of the devices named
post.description: Returns, for each non-revoked device of the user, its newest unexpired unconsumed ordinary package (marking it consumed) or, when that device's pool is empty, its newest unexpired last-resort package (not consumed). `deviceIds` narrows the claim to those devices (1 to 64 ids; an empty list is 400, never "all"): it is a filter over the active devices, not a demand, so an id that is unknown, revoked, another person's, or has no package to give is absent from the answer (the same for each; compare the answer's `deviceId`s with what you asked for), and no other device's package is touched. Without it, every active device answers. Either way the rows come oldest device first. Every claim is recorded: a commit may later add a device only with a package that its own committer claimed. Claims are limited per calling device (30 per 10 minutes, 429 CLAIM_RATE_LIMITED), per calling user across all of their devices (60, 429 ACTOR_RATE_LIMITED) and per target user across all callers (60, 429 TARGET_RATE_LIMITED; claiming your own packages is not counted against the target; naming devices changes none of the budgets), with `Retry-After`: an unlimited claim is a way to drain a victim's pool. Only the owner, an admin of the owner (`adminOf`) or a contact (a device that shares or shared a room with one of the user's devices) may claim; the operator's packages (the account that owns every ASSISTANT device) are claimable by every device. Anyone else gets 403 NOT_A_CONTACT, checked after the limits and before any package is handed out.

post.summary: Append a commit to the conversation, in epoch order
post.description: The epoch serializer (ADR-117 §2). A commit must be built on the current epoch: `expectedEpoch` ≠ current → 409 `{currentEpoch}`; rebase on what won and resend. After 5 consecutive losses the answer is 429 REBASE_LIMIT. Safe to retry: the same device resending the same bytes for the same `expectedEpoch` after it was stored gets 200 and the original receipt. `kind` other than COMMIT (a standalone proposal) is 422 HANDSHAKE_KIND_UNSUPPORTED: propose inside a commit. `bytes` must be an MLSMessage (a PublicMessage from a member, or a PrivateMessage) for this room's group and current epoch with content type commit, else 422 MLS_HEADER_MISMATCH naming the field; a `welcome` must parse as a Welcome. The relay reads only that cleartext header, never the content. `memberDelta` says who the commit adds and removes, and is stored and returned by GET: removing a GUARDIAN device needs a FAMILY_ADMIN token whose `adminOf` lists the child, or another GUARDIAN device of the same child driven by a token whose `guardianOf` lists the child (403), adding a device that is revoked (422 DEVICE_REVOKED) or not on its owner's signed list (422 DEVICE_NOT_IN_SIGNED_LIST) is refused, and each added device must name the `keyPackageId` that THIS device claimed for it (422 KEY_PACKAGE_NOT_CLAIMED_BY_COMMITTER). A device a commit removed gets 403 REMOVED. There is no groupInfo: external joins are out of scope, and an unknown field is a 400. `senderDeviceId` must be the token's device.

get.summary: Read the conversation's handshake log, in order
get.description: Members, and devices a commit removed. Returns messages built on epoch `fromEpoch` or later, after `afterSeq`. A device never sees handshakes older than the one that added it (or the epoch before it, which holds its own Welcome). A removed device reads up to and including the commit that removed it, with `removedAtEpoch` set, and then gets 403 REMOVED. Each commit carries the `memberDelta` its sender declared; compare it with what the decrypted commit really does. `oldestAvailableSeq` says where retention cut the log.

schema.description: A page of handshakes.

bytes.description: An MLS handshake message (base64, at most 262144 bytes decoded)

memberDelta.description: What the sender DECLARED the commit adds and removes, exactly as posted; null on a WELCOME. The relay cannot read the commit: every member must compare this with the changes the decrypted commit really makes, and treat a difference as an attack.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `afterSeq` to read the next page; null when there is none.

oldestAvailableSeq.description: The lowest seq the relay still holds (older rows were deleted by retention), or the next seq it will hand out when it holds none. A cursor below `oldestAvailableSeq - 1` has missed rows that no longer exist: recover from the group state, not by paging.

removedAtEpoch.description: Set for a device a commit removed: its reading ends before this epoch (it still sees the commit that removed it). Once nothing is left in that window the answer is 403 REMOVED.

post.summary: Append an encrypted message to the conversation
post.description: The relay stores `ciphertext` as given and cannot read it. The sender must be a current member (403 NOT_A_MEMBER, or REMOVED for a device a commit removed) and `epoch` must be the group's current epoch, else 409 `{currentEpoch}`: the message was encrypted for a group that no longer exists. The ciphertext must be an MLS PrivateMessage of this room's group and that epoch with content type application, else 422 MLS_HEADER_MISMATCH naming the field (the relay reads only that cleartext header). Safe to retry with `clientMsgId`: the same device sending the same id again gets 200 and the original seq (409 CLIENT_MSG_ID_REUSED if the ciphertext differs).

ciphertext.description: An MLS application message (base64, at most 65536 bytes decoded)

clientMsgId.description: The sender's own id for this message, unique per sending device.

200.description: A retry (same `clientMsgId`, same ciphertext): the original seq.
